HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces that it has initiated RANOVA, a registrational Phase III clinical trial of ranosidenib (HMPL-306) in patients with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 gliomas harboring isocitrate dehydrogenase (“IDH”) 1 or 2 mutations in China. Ranosidenib is a novel, highly potent and selective dual inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. The first patient received the first dose on November 20, 2026.

Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, representing around 80% of all primary malignant and central nervous system tumors.1 Worldwide, it is estimated that approximately 260,000 new cases of glioma are diagnosed annually, including nearly 70,000 in China. 2,3 IDH1 or IDH2 mutations are recognized as key oncogenic drivers in the pathogenesis and progression of glioma, found in approximately 70% to 80% of Grade 2 or 3 gliomas, including astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma.4

The trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III study evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral ranosidenib versus placebo in participants with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations who have previously received only surgical treatment. Following Blinded Independent Review Committee (“BIRC”)-confirmed disease progression, eligible participants in the placebo group may cross over to receive ranosidenib.

The primary outcome measure is progression-free survival (“PFS”) assessed by BIRC according to Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) 2.0 criteria. Secondary outcome measures include investigator-assessed PFS, time to next intervention (TTNI), tumor growth rate (TGR), objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), safety, and quality of life. Additional details may be found at clinicaltrials.gov, using identifier NCT07912398.

This registrational trial plans to enroll approximately 210 patients in China. The leading principal investigators are Professor Jinsong Wu of Huashan Hospital, Fudan University and Professor Xiaohui Ren of Capital Medical University Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

About Ranosidenib

Ranosidenib is a novel dual-inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. Mutations of IDH1 and IDH2 have been implicated as drivers of certain hematological malignancies, gliomas and solid tumors. Cytoplasmic mutant IDH1 and mitochondrial mutant IDH2 have been known to switch to the other form when targeted by an inhibitor of IDH1 mutant alone or IDH2 mutant alone. Targeting both IDH1 and IDH2 mutations may provide therapeutic benefits in cancer patients by overcoming this acquired resistance.

HUTCHMED currently retains all rights to ranosidenib worldwide.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM:HCM; HKEX:13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first five medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan. For more information, please visit: www.hutch-med.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alps Group Inc (“Alps” or “the Company”) (Nasdaq: ALPS), an integrated biotechnology platform headquartered in Malaysia, today announced that it has received written notification from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) confirming that the Company has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on The Nasdaq Global Market.

On May 19, 2026, the Company previously disclosed that, on May 15, 2026, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq notifying the Company that based on the closing bid price of the ordinary shares of the Company for the prior 30 consecutive business days, the Company was not in compliance with the continued listing requirement of Nasdaq under Nasdaq Listing Rules 5450(a)(1), which requires the Company to maintain a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share.

On November 9, 2026, the Company’s ordinary shares began trading on a post-consolidation basis following the Company’s previously announced 1-for-5 share consolidation.

On November 16, 2026, the Company received a letter from the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff stating that the Company had not regained compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1), which required the listed ordinary shares to maintain a closing bid price of $1.00 per share for 10 consecutive business days, by November 11, 2026, the end of the applicable compliance period, and that the Staff had determined that the Company’s ordinary shares would be subject to delisting.

On November 20, 2026, the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff notified the Company that the closing bid price of its ordinary shares had been $1.00 per share or greater for 10 consecutive business days, from November 9, 2026 to November 20, 2026. Accordingly, the Company has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement, and Nasdaq has confirmed that the matter is now closed.

The notification has no effect on the trading of the Company’s ordinary shares which continue to trade on The Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol “ALPS.”

About Alps Group Inc

Alps Group Inc is a revenue-generating integrated biotechnology platform headquartered in Malaysia, operating across cell manufacturing, molecular diagnostics, and clinical delivery. Alps leverages revenue from its commercial businesses to support its clinical pipeline development, with a mission to make advanced precision medicine accessible and affordable across Southeast Asia.

Received highly favorable notification from the FDA on 56 PMTA SKUs for inclusion on a list of products against which FDA does not intend to prioritize enforcement

PACHA age-gated products will be America's first age-gated disposables

COSTA MESA, CA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Charlie’s Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CHUC) (“Charlie’s” or the “Company”), an industry leader in the premium vapor products space, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on recent business highlights.

Key Financial Highlights for First Nine Months 2026 (compared to first nine months 2025)

  • Revenue increased 19% to $11.3 million
  • Gross profit decreased 3% to $2.4 million
  • Operating loss increased 75% to $3.9 million

Key Balance Sheet Highlights as of September 30, 2026 (compared to December 2025)

  • Cash balance of $0.4 million, compared to $1.3 million
  • Total assets of $11.2 million, compared to $11.6 million
  • Total stockholders’ equity of $1.4 million, compared to $3.4 million

Management Commentary

“Because billions of dollars of illicit vapor products – made by Chinese manufacturers who thumb their noses at the FDA – have flooded the United States this year, Charlie’s sales and profits have taken a hit,” reported Henry Sicignano, President and CEO. “Fortunately, we have the inventory, and the opportunity, to reestablish growing, profitable sales in several states where regulatory enforcement has again become a priority. In this environment, we have redoubled our commitment to regulatory compliance as well as our initiatives to monetize the Company’s 678-SKU PMTA portfolio.”

Mr. Sicignano continued, “Big Tobacco ‘pod systems’ are outdated, provide very low puff counts, and offer few flavor choices. Charlie’s products are modern disposable products… offering much higher puff counts… and hundreds of flavors that adult consumers strongly prefer. For all these reasons, we believe Charlie’s PACHA product line is the best, most robust portfolio of PMTA products in the industry and will likely represent significant value to one or more Big Tobacco strategic partners in 2027.”

As previously reported, Charlie’s has made the well-considered decision to focus intensely on the two strategic priorities that matter most to Company shareholders:

1) Management has shifted its priorities from sales of the PACHAMAMA and SBX product lines to a laser focus on the beta test pilot of PACHA age-gated disposables. The Company has already received tens of thousands of finished age-gated PACHA products in its warehouse. Management has secured test-market purchase commitments from retailers. As soon as the Company’s software licensor completes final tests of its “second generation” consumer app, Charlie’s will begin shipping the age-gated PACHA product to stores. The Company expects that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

2) The Company has redeployed the priorities of one of Charlie’s largest shareholders. Ryan Stump, Charlie’s co-founder and former COO, has begun work to identify and pursue strategic transactions and/or partnerships with leading global tobacco companies to significantly enhance long-term value for Charlie’s shareholders.

Regulatory Developments

FDA Enforcement Priorities Guidance

In August 2026, the FDA notified Charlie’s that certain of its PACHA products (56 SKUs) for which PMTAs have been submitted have been tentatively identified for inclusion on the FDA's public-facing webpage of products for which the FDA generally does not intend to prioritize enforcement of premarket authorization requirements — a development the Company views as highly favorable. Inclusion on the FDA’s new list of “low-enforcement priority products” does not, however, constitute FDA marketing authorization, preclude case-by-case enforcement, or bear on whether any PMTA will ultimately be granted. Accordingly, Charlie’s intends to continue pursuing FDA review of its pending PMTAs and to comply with all applicable requirements.

FDA has validated age-gating as a pathway for the legal sale of flavored Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (“ENDS”) products

In May 2026, the FDA granted marketing orders for four Glas Inc. pod products, including “Gold” (mango) and “Sapphire” (blueberry) flavored, age-gated pods. This landmark development validates “age-gating” as a legitimate pathway for the legal sale of flavored ENDS products in the United States. However, Juul Labs filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Glas, Inc. and, under these circumstances, Glas’ newly authorized “fruit flavored” products are unlikely to go on the market in the near term; it is likely that Charlie’s PACHA age-gated products will be America’s first age-gated disposables.

Business Catalysts

Charlie’s plans to begin beta testing PACHA age-gated flavored disposables.

In December 2025, the Company signed a definitive licensing agreement to commercialize the first-ever AI-powered blockchain-based age-gating system for vapor products in the United States. Scheduled to beta test this year, the PACHA test-market initiative will incorporate the age-gating system in a special line of the Company’s flavored ENDS disposables; simultaneously, Charlie’s intends to amend certain of its existing PMTAs with the FDA for PACHA brand ENDS with the youth access prevention system.

Mr. Sicignano commented, “Charlie’s plans to launch PACHA products that have not yet received final FDA authorization follows the example set by one of America’s largest tobacco companies… In recent months, RJ Reynolds' Vuse business began selling four new fruit flavor pods (berry, fresh mint, peach, and watermelon), all of which were issued FDA Marketing Denial Orders (MDOs). Given that Reynolds has demonstrated it is willing to pursue flavored ENDS commercialization strategies, before final FDA authorization, we believe the strategic calculus for Charlie’s – and for our potential strategic partners – has improved. Dramatically.”

Charlie’s will monetize the Company’s PMTAs through new strategic partnerships

In 2025, in three separate transactions, Charlie's sold sixteen of the Company's PACHA synthetic nicotine PMTA products and related assets for $7.5 million in cash plus a contingent one-time payment of up to $4.2 million. In the last of the three transactions, the buyer purchased a single Charlie’s PMTA product for $1 million. Based on these sales, taking into account the fact that Charlie’s continues to own 678 PMTA products, and considering the interest other companies have expressed in Charlie's portfolio, the Company believes Charlie's remaining PMTA products, as a stand-alone asset, could have a monetary value that significantly exceeds the Company’s current market cap.

Financial Results for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue: For the three months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $2.7 million, a decrease of $3.4 million, or 56%, compared with $6.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This decrease was primarily due to a significant decrease in sales of the SBX product line, from ongoing inconsistency in regulatory enforcement affecting customers’ desire for non-nicotine based vapor products. The decline in sales was offset by the launch of USA-made Pachamama line and sales of Pacha disposable products that are still under substantive review with FDA.

  • Gross Profit: For the three months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $0.1 million, a decrease of $1.5 million, or 92%, compared with $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Total Operating Expenses: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $1.8 million, a decrease of $0.2 million, or 10%, compared with $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Operating Loss: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $1.7 million, compared with an operating loss of $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Financial Results for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Revenue: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 revenue was $11.3 million, an increase of $1.8 million, or 19%, compared with $9.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was all due to the increase in nicotine-based product and nicotine alternative products sales. Sales of SBX, a non-nicotine, disposable vapor product which is not subject to FDA review, experienced a significant increase in the early part of 2026.

  • Gross Profit: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026 gross profit was $2.4 million, a decrease of $0.1 million, or 3%, compared with $2.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Total Operating Expenses: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total operating expenses, including general and administrative, sales and marketing and research and development costs, were $6.3 million, an increase of $1.6 million, or 34%, compared with $4.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

  • Operating Loss: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating loss was $3.9 million, compared with an operating loss of $2.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

About Charlie’s Holdings, Inc.

Charlie's Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CHUC) is an industry leader in the premium vapor products space. The Company's products are sold around the world to select distributors, specialty retailers, and third-party online resellers through subsidiary company Charlie's Chalk Dust, LLC. Charlie's Chalk Dust has developed an extensive portfolio of brand styles, flavor profiles, and innovative product formats.

For additional information, please visit Charlie’s corporate website at: Chuc.com and the Company’s branded online websites: sbxvape.com, CharliesChalkDust.com, enjoypachamama.com, and Pacha.co.

Third-quarter revenue of $11.2 million increased from $8.2 million in the second quarter; year-over-year results continued to reflect lower residential demand following the expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit.

Commercial revenue increased 20% year-over-year to $2.7 million; SG&A expense declined 37% year-over-year to $4.3 million.

Results included $9.8 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges.

SUNation continues to prioritize liquidity, cost management, and execution of its proposed merger with Suniva.

RONKONKOMA, N.Y., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SUNation Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: SUNE) (“SUNation” or the “Company”), a leading provider of residential and commercial solar energy systems, battery storage solutions and comprehensive energy services, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3 2026”).

Third-quarter revenue increased sequentially to $11.2 million from $8.2 million, and gross margin improved to 30.8% from 26.1%, reflecting higher revenue across the Company’s New York and Hawaii operations. Year-over-year performance continued to reflect downward pressure from the residential solar market’s adjustment to the expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit at the end of 2025 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (“OBBBA”). Consolidated revenue declined 41% year over year, with lower residential revenue partially offset by growth in commercial revenue.

SUNation Reduces Costs and Advances Suniva Merger

The Company continued to manage its cost structure, reducing selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expense by 37% year over year. Results also included $9.8 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges following an assessment of asset recoverability in light of lower forecast revenue and operating results. Including these charges, SUNation reported an operating loss of $11.7 million and a net loss of $11.8 million.

SUNation also continued to advance its proposed reverse merger with Suniva, Inc. (“Suniva”). SUNation currently anticipates closing in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction or waiver of applicable closing conditions and receipt of required approvals and regulatory clearances.

Q3 2026 HIGHLIGHTS

  • Revenue and gross margin improved sequentially
    Revenue increased to $11.2 million from $8.2 million in Q2 2026, and gross margin improved to 30.8% from 26.1%. Revenue declined 41% year over year, primarily reflecting lower residential installation activity.
  • Commercial revenue grew 20% year over year
    Commercial revenue reached $2.66 million, compared with $2.23 million in Q3 2025, primarily driven by growth in New York.
  • SG&A expense declined 37% year over year
    SG&A expense decreased to $4.33 million from $6.90 million, reflecting lower selling and marketing expenses and personnel cost reductions.
  • Net loss reflected non-cash impairment charges
    Net loss was $11.82 million, compared with $0.39 million in Q3 2025. Results included $9.82 million of non-cash goodwill and intangible asset impairment charges reflecting lower forecast revenue and operating results.
  • Suniva merger process advanced
    The companies amended their merger agreement during the quarter to address financing, stockholder approvals and closing requirements. Closing is currently anticipated in Q1 2027, subject to applicable conditions and approvals.

Commercial Growth Supports Revenue Diversification

The quarter’s sequential revenue and gross-margin improvement occurred within a residential market that continued to operate below prior-year activity levels. Residential revenue declined 52% year over year, while commercial revenue increased 20%. Commercial and service revenue together represented approximately 33% of consolidated revenue, compared with approximately 18% in Q3 2025.

The prior-year quarter also benefited from residential demand ahead of the year-end 2025 tax credit expiration, contributing to the year-over-year comparison. Management continues to emphasize commercial projects, battery storage, service and adjacent energy offerings as part of its efforts to diversify revenue.

Storage Opportunities Support Adaptation to Residential Market Changes

The expiration of the Section 25D federal residential tax credit at year-end 2025 under OBBBA continued to affect residential demand, installation volumes and financing economics during Q3 2026, following elevated activity ahead of the expiration. Lower installation volumes also increased fixed labor and overhead costs as a percentage of revenue.

Battery storage remains an area of focus. Hawaii’s Bring Your Own Device Plus program provides incentives for qualifying customers to add storage to existing or new rooftop solar systems. Hawaii Energy Connection’s battery attachment rates increased 13% year over year during the quarter.

Updated Asset Values and Liquidity Priorities

The Company’s impairment assessment reflected a material reduction in forecast revenue and operating results. Goodwill impairment charges related to the SUNation Residential and SUNation Commercial reporting units, while intangible asset impairment charges related to tradenames and trademarks across the New York and Hawaii businesses.

SUNation continues to prioritize cash preservation, disciplined working capital management and additional financing to support operations and maintain financial flexibility. The Company ended the quarter with $2.79 million in cash and cash equivalents and requires additional capital to meet its obligations and operating needs.

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY

“Third-quarter revenue and gross margin improved from the second quarter as activity increased across our New York and Hawaii businesses,” said Scott Maskin, Chief Executive Officer of SUNation. “Commercial revenue grew 20% year over year, and commercial and service work represented a larger share of our business. Residential demand continues to reflect the change in customer economics following the expiration of the federal residential tax credit, and our teams remain focused on matching our offerings and operating structure to the market we are serving.”

Mr. Maskin continued, “Our priorities remain disciplined execution, customer service, cost management and liquidity. We are pursuing commercial projects, storage installations, service work, roofing and adjacent energy opportunities while managing expenses closely. We also continued to advance the Suniva merger process during the quarter, including an amendment to the merger agreement addressing financing and closing-related matters.”

James Brennan, SUNation’s Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operations Officer, said, “Higher sequential revenue supported gross-margin improvement to 30.8%, while year-over-year SG&A expense declined 37% following reductions in selling, marketing and personnel costs. Our reported results also included $9.8 million of non-cash impairment charges reflecting the effect of lower forecast revenue and operating results on the carrying value of goodwill and intangible assets.”

Mr. Brennan added, “Cash preservation, working capital management and access to additional capital remain essential. We ended September with $2.8 million of cash and cash equivalents, and our working capital position continues to require close management. We are evaluating financing sources and managing our obligations while supporting customer commitments and the proposed transaction.”

Mr. Maskin concluded, “We currently anticipate completing the Suniva merger in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the required conditions and approvals. Our immediate responsibility is to operate the business carefully through that process, serve our customers and preserve financial flexibility. The experience of our teams in New York and Hawaii, our customer relationships and our range of energy services remain important foundations as we navigate the current market.”

Q3 2026 FINANCIAL AND OPERATIONAL RESULTS

FINANCIAL RESULTS

  • Revenue
    Consolidated revenue was $11.20 million, compared with $18.99 million in Q3 2025, a decrease of 41%. Residential contract revenue declined 52%, partially offset by 20% growth in commercial revenue.
  • Gross profit and margin
    Gross profit was $3.45 million, compared with $7.21 million in Q3 2025. Gross margin was 30.8%, compared with 38.0% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting lower revenue and fixed labor and overhead costs that declined more slowly than sales volume. Gross profit and margin improved sequentially from approximately $2.1 million and 26.1%, respectively, in Q2 2026.
  • Operating expenses and cost reductions

SG&A expense declined 37% to $4.33 million from $6.90 million, reflecting lower selling and marketing expenses and personnel cost reductions.
  • Net loss
    Net loss was $11.82 million, or $1.81 per basic and diluted share, compared with $0.39 million, or $0.12 per basic and diluted share, in Q3 2025. The increase reflected the impairment charges and lower gross profit, partially offset by reduced SG&A expense. Operating loss was $11.71 million, compared with $0.25 million in Q3 2025. Impairment charges comprised $4.92 million of goodwill and $4.90 million of intangible assets. Amortization expense was unchanged year over year at $0.56 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, revenue was $26.56 million, gross profit was $7.17 million and SG&A expense was $13.87 million, compared with $44.69 million, $16.48 million and $19.38 million, respectively, in the prior-year period. The following comparisons are with December 31, 2025, unless otherwise indicated.

  • Payables and loans payable
    Accounts payable declined 23% to $5.66 million from $7.40 million. The aggregate carrying amount of current and long-term loans payable and related interest, including related-party balances, declined to $4.98 million from $6.60 million, reflecting repayments, the related-party debt conversion completed earlier in 2026 and borrowings under the affiliated revolving credit facility.
  • Credit facility extension
    On October 15, 2026, the maturity of the Company’s $1.5 million affiliated revolving credit facility was extended to April 15, 2027. Total liabilities were $22.78 million, compared with $23.90 million at year-end. The Company requires additional capital resources and is considering all available options, including the ongoing strategic initiatives previously announced. The availability, timing, and terms of any additional funding remains undetermined.

SUNation continued to advance its proposed reverse merger with Suniva during Q3 2026. The transaction, announced in June following the Board’s review of strategic alternatives, would result in Suniva becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of SUNation.

Late-breaking 1-year data in 100 patients presented at PCR London Valves 2026: No moderate or severe paravalvular leak, 96% in NYHA class I/II and 97% free from moderate or severe prosthesis-patient mismatch at 30 days

MINNEAPOLIS and BRISBANE, Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Anteris Technologies Global Corp. (“Anteris” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: AVR, ASX: AVR) today announced 1-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes for the DurAVR® Transcatheter Heart Valve (THV) in 100 patients with severe aortic stenosis and small aortic annuli (annulus area 404 ± 37 mm2), the anatomy in which transcatheter valves most often leave patients with elevated gradients and prosthesis-patient mismatch* (PPM).

At 1 year, 1% of patients had been hospitalized for heart failure. DurAVR THV maintained a mean pressure gradient of 8.9 mmHg and a mean effective orifice area (EOA) of 2.2 cm2, with no moderate or severe paravalvular leak (PVL) observed and no valve-related mortality reported. At 30 days, 97% of patients were free from moderate or severe PPM. Symptoms improved substantially: the proportion of patients who achieved New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I/II rose from 39% at baseline to 96% at 1 year.

These results were achieved in a symptomatic and clinically complex population. At baseline, 61% of patients were in NYHA class III/IV, the mean STS-PROM score was 4.7 ± 4.0%, and the cohort included heavy calcification and bicuspid anatomy (9%). Patients were pooled from the EMBARK and early feasibility studies (EFS) conducted in the United States and Europe; previously, 30-day data from this cohort were presented at PCR London Valves 2025.

The late-breaking abstract, titled “One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes of a Novel Biomimetic Balloon-Expandable THV in Small Aortic Annuli,” was presented by Rishi Puri, MD, PhD, of Cleveland Clinic, during the TAVI Hotline – Part 1 session at PCR London Valves on Sunday, November 22, 2026.

1 Year Results Highlights

  • Heart failure hospitalization: 1% at 1 year compares favorably to mid-to-high single-digit rates reported in contemporary clinical trials with currently marketed products.1,2
  • Hemodynamics: Mean pressure gradient fell from 48.1 ± 17.0 mmHg at baseline to 8.9 ± 4.3 mmHg at 1 year, and mean EOA increased from 0.8 ± 0.2 cm2 to 2.2 ± 0.9 cm2. These results were similar to those reported at 30 days in 2025.
  • Hemodynamic Valve Deterioration: No moderate or severe hemodynamic valve deterioration was observed at 1 year.
  • Valve performance: No moderate or severe PVL was observed and no valve-related deaths were reported through 1 year.
  • Symptoms: Patients in NYHA class I/II increased from 39% at baseline to 96% at 1 year, and 81% of patients experienced symptom improvement.
  • Clinical events at 1 year: All-cause mortality 6% (2 CV mortalities; 2 non-cardiac infections; 1 cancer; 1 car accident), stroke 3% and new permanent pacemaker implantation 9%.
  • Cardiac remodeling: In a cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy (n = 64), left ventricular (LV) mass, a marker of modifying the underlying disease, regressed by 24% at 1 year. LV mass in the patients evaluated was similar to that reported in matched controls without aortic valve disease3. These findings are consistent with sustained unloading of the left ventricle.

“Small aortic annuli are where we most often see elevated gradients and mismatch after TAVR, and these patients are disproportionately women. In this symptomatic cohort, DurAVR delivered single-digit gradients, no moderate or greater paravalvular leak and 97% freedom from moderate or severe mismatch at 30 days. While cross-trial comparisons should be interpreted with caution, what stands out to me is heart failure hospitalization of just 1% at one year. These patients had a mean STS score of 4.7%, and most were in NYHA class III or IV, yet 1% is well below the hospitalization rates reported in contemporary clinical trials with currently marketed products. These are encouraging results, and the randomized PARADIGM trial is the right next test,” said Rishi Puri, MD, PhD, Interventional Cardiologist, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, United States.

“Small annuli are the hardest test in TAVR, and these patients were symptomatic, with 61% in NYHA class III or IV at baseline. At one year, heart failure hospitalization was just 1%, a fraction of the rate typically observed after valve replacement. Heart failure admissions are the event patients feel most, health systems pay for most and that most closely predicts mortality. The cardiac MRI data show why DurAVR is different: with single-digit gradients and no moderate or severe paravalvular leak, left ventricular mass regressed by 24%, which tells us the heart is unloading and beginning to remodel. We believe DurAVR's biomimetic design and its potential to restore more physiologic blood flow may contribute to improved cardiac remodeling. These findings are consistent with that hypothesis, and PARADIGM is designed to test DurAVR head-to-head against today’s commercial valves. These results give us strong conviction going into the pivotal trial,” said Chris Meduri, MD, MPH, Chief Medical Officer of Anteris.

“Reducing heart failure hospitalization is among the most consequential events after aortic valve replacement, due to its proven correlation with CV mortality. In a pooled analysis of more than 3,400 patients treated with TAVR or surgical aortic valve replacement in the PARTNER trials, the 1-year heart failure hospitalization rate was 6.7%, and these hospitalizations were associated with increased mortality.1 In the randomized SMART trial of small-annulus patients at lower predicted risk (mean STS-PROM 3.3%), 1-year heart failure hospitalization was 4.1% with the Evolut valve and 3.5% with the SAPIEN valve.2 Against this backdrop, our current dataset gives us great confidence for the ongoing pivotal PARADIGM study where cardiovascular hospitalization is also a component of the primary endpoint,” said Wayne Paterson, Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Anteris.

The DurAVR THV is being studied in the pivotal PARADIGM Trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT07194265), a randomized, head-to-head comparison against commercially available TAVR valves that is actively enrolling patients across the United States and Europe.

1Huded CP, et al. Circ Cardiovasc Interv. 2022;15(12):e012195.

2Herrmann HC, et al. Self-Expanding or Balloon-Expandable TAVR in Patients with a Small Aortic Annulus. N Engl J Med. 2024;390:1959-1971. Component rates (Kaplan-Meier) from SMART results posted at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04722250.

3Garg P, et al. European Heart Journal, Valvular & Structural Disease; 2026.

*Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) occurs when an implanted valve’s effective opening is too small for the patient’s body size, resulting in higher-than-expected gradients. PPM is common after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with small aortic annuli and has been associated with reduced long-term survival after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

About the PARADIGM Trial

This head-to-head study will enroll approximately 1,000 patients in the ‘All Comers Randomized Cohort' with 1:1 randomization of patients who will receive either the DurAVR THV or TAVR using commercially available and approved THVs. On its stand, Schneider Electric will demonstrate how Industrial Intelligence and Open, Software-Defined Automation connect data and AI with machine and process control. Visitors will also see how energy and operational data can be managed together, rather than as separate challenges.

They need the ability to turn intelligence into action,” says Gwenaelle Huet, executive vice president of Industrial Automation at Schneider Electric. “That is why we believe automation must be open and software-defined: it lets customers bring energy, AI and operations together, and keep evolving without replacing the investments they have already made.”

Advancing Open, Software-Defined Automation

New collaboration and development features reduce the time spent on engineering and integration. Support for open APIs, Visual Studio Code and Python lets engineers keep using the tools they already know.

The release also gives customers more flexibility to modernize and update critical systems while minimizing disruption to operations. A new web-native HMI enables browser-based visualization and maintenance. Expanded online-change and high-availability capabilities let systems evolve progressively, without replacing automation investments that are still viable.

More open access to automation data also makes it easier to connect external AI tools and introduce AI-assisted engineering and operations. For machine builders, this means faster engineering and greater reuse across machine portfolios. For industrial operators, it offers a practical way to add new software and intelligence capabilities as their operations evolve.

With EcoStruxure Automation Expert already deployed at more than 900 customer sites worldwide, Schneider Electric is demonstrating how open, software-defined automation runs industrial operations today.

To accelerate adoption of open, software-defined automation, we are introducing Automate 360: the unified environment and foundational layer across control and compute that underpins EcoStruxure Automation Expert. The Project comprises 12 mineral claims covering 3,646.90 hectares (approximately 9,011.7 acres) and two pending mineral claim applications covering an additional 746.86 hectares (approximately 1,845.5 acres). Together, the claims and applications cover 4,393.76 hectares (approximately 10,857.2 acres).

Quatum is located near the Company’s 100%-owned Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project on West Redonda Island. The historical CAP showing in the Quatum area lies approximately 13 kilometres (8 miles) north-northeast of the RED occurrence at Redonda. This proximity provides an opportunity to evaluate coordinated exploration planning and regional logistics, while building on Copper One’s experience at Redonda.1

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “Quatum represents an exciting opportunity for Copper One to advance a copper-bearing breccia system previously explored by Newmont. Its historical drilling and surface mineralization provide a compelling foundation for renewed exploration using modern techniques. Its proximity to our ongoing drilling at the 100%-owned Redonda Project, previously explored by Teck, strengthens the strategic fit and creates opportunities to apply our regional geological knowledge and coordinate exploration activities. Together, these projects expand our presence in British Columbia and reinforce our strategy of building a substantial North American copper portfolio. With projects across Nevada, Utah and British Columbia, Copper One is assembling multiple opportunities for discovery and growth as the world’s need for copper continues to expand.”

Quatum Project highlights

  • Government records document three diamond drill holes completed by Newmont in 1970, totaling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres). 

  • Historical copper mineralization associated with an intrusive breccia system near the CAP showing, with chalcopyrite and locally observed bornite. 

  • Historical Hole 1 results include 0.17% copper over 100 feet (30.48 metres), with a higher-grade interval of 0.38% copper over 10 feet (3.05 metres). These are historical reported results requiring verification. 

  • Historical surface chip sampling at location J returned a reported weighted average of 0.46% copper over 20 feet (6.10 metres). True widths are unknown. 

  • Historical mapping, soil sampling and geophysical surveys provide a basis for evaluating targets for follow-up exploration. 

Historical exploration and geological setting

The British Columbia Geological Survey identifies the CAP or QUATUM RIVER showing as a copper showing classified as a porphyry copper occurrence hosted by intrusive rocks of the Coast Plutonic Complex. Its description records chalcopyrite, pyrite and pyrrhotite mainly within a breccia pipe hosted by quartz monzonite and quartz diorite.2

British Columbia’s Geology, Exploration and Mining 1970 (p. 229) records three surface diamond drill holes totalling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres) on the Cap 2 claim, together with geological mapping, 6.6 line-miles (approximately 10.6 line-kilometres) of magnetometer and induced polarization surveys, and 296 soil samples.3

Historical information and data verification

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for rare diseases, today announced that it received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its resubmitted Biologics License Application (BLA) for Deramiocel, its investigational cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies.

“We are deeply disappointed for the boys and young men living with Duchenne and their families,” said Linda Marbán, Ph.D., Capricor’s Chief Executive Officer. “Deramiocel has been studied in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, HOPE-2 and HOPE-3, both of which met their primary endpoints. We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval. We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.”

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of approximately $198.5 million, which it believes is sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months. About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited.

About Deramiocel

Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe.

About Capricor Therapeutics

Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, evaluated in clinical studies for its potential to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. HALIFAX, NS, Nov. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Isar Aerospace ("Isar") and Maritime Launch Services ("MLS") (TSX: MAXQ) (OTCQB: MAXQF) are taking the next step in advancing Canadian space capabilities with the transition of a dedicated launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia to Isar. This marks the moment at which Isar assumes operational responsibility for its own launch infrastructure on Canadian soil and the beginning of construction on what will become Isar's dedicated launch pad in Canada.

The handover is a key milestone in the two companies' partnership, under which Isar will develop, build and operate a dedicated launch complex, including a final assembly line and a payload preparation facility, for its Spectrum launch vehicle. First orbital launches are targeted for 2028. The announcement comes with the support of the Canadian government, reflecting shared priorities in sovereign space capability and defence cooperation.

In September this year, Isar successfully reached orbit on its second mission, becoming the first European commercial space company to deliver satellites into orbit. As the company ramps up production of its in-house-developed launch vehicle at its purpose-built factory near Munich – with capacity of 40 vehicles per year – it is also expanding its global launch site network. Spaceport Nova Scotia will be Isar's second launch site globally, and its first in North America.

"Starting construction on our launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia brings us a decisive step closer to launching from Canadian soil. But our ambition goes far beyond building a launch site. Together with Maritime Launch Services, we want to advance Canada's space ecosystem and establish sovereign access to orbit as a lasting national capability – one that strengthens Canada's role as a space nation and the Alliance's capabilities for years to come," said Stella Guillen, Chief Commercial Officer of Isar Aerospace.

"Today's handover marks an important step in the development of Spaceport Nova Scotia and demonstrates the strength of our multi-user spaceport model. Isar Aerospace's investment advances sovereign launch capability in Canada, strengthens cooperation between allies, and brings foreign direct investment and jobs to Nova Scotia and the communities surrounding the spaceport. It also strengthens Nova Scotia's position in the global space economy and Canada's role as a spacefaring nation," said Stephen Matier, President and CEO of Maritime Launch Services.

Spaceport Nova Scotia, developed by Maritime Launch Services Inc., is a multi-user orbital launch facility, located near the rural communities of Canso, Hazel Hill and Little Dover. Designed to support multiple launch providers and customers, its location on Nova Scotia's Atlantic coast provides over-ocean launch trajectories and access to mid- to high-inclination and polar orbits. The site will support Earth observation, communications and defence missions for government and commercial operators alike.

Isar's investment aligns directly with Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy and the Canadian Space Launch Act, both of which identify and prioritize sovereign launch capability as a national priority. As a company that designs, manufactures and operates its own launch vehicles, Isar brings integrated end-to-end launch expertise to a facility built to support Canadian and allied missions.

"Canada's sovereignty extends beyond our borders and into space. This partnership between Maritime Launch Services and Germany's Isar Aerospace is an important step toward building a sovereign space-launch capability right here in Canada. It will strengthen our national security, create new opportunities for Canadian industry, and deepen our defence cooperation with Germany. As space becomes increasingly critical to our security and our economy, Canada must have the ability to launch and protect the capabilities we depend on," said the Honourable David J. McGuinty, Minister of National Defence.

"Companies are turning to Nova Scotia to make world-class ideas into solutions, showing Nova Scotia's unique strength in the aerospace and defence sector. Congratulations to Isar and Maritime Launch Services for advancing critical launch infrastructure that will strengthen Canada's position in the global space economy and create high-value opportunities for Nova Scotians well beyond the launch pad", said the Honourable Colton LeBlanc, Minister of Growth, Development and Defence Industries, Province of Nova Scotia.

About Isar Aerospace
The European space company Isar Aerospace offers launch services for transporting small and medium-sized satellites and satellite constellations into Earth orbit. The launch vehicles used to transport these satellites are developed, manufactured, and tested almost entirely in-house. Headquartered near Munich, Germany, Isar Aerospace was founded in 2018 and has grown to over 400 employees, working across 5 international locations. Private funding from international investors provides strong backing for the company's pioneering approach to scale and industrialize launch vehicle production through vertical integration.
More information: www.isaraerospace.com

About Maritime Launch Services Inc.
Maritime Launch (TSX: MAXQ, OTCQB: MAXQF) is a Canadian-owned commercial space company based in Nova Scotia. Maritime Launch is developing Spaceport Nova Scotia, a dual-use, multi-user spaceport designed to support civil and defence-related space missions. From a single site, Spaceport Nova Scotia will enable launch vehicles to place satellites into low Earth orbit across a broad range of orbital inclinations, from 45 to 98 degrees.

The Consent Solicitation was made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Issuer’s Consent Solicitation Statement, dated November 16, 2026 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated November 16, 2026, and Amendment No. 2 thereto, dated November 18, 2026, the “Consent Solicitation Statement”).

The Consent Solicitation expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 20, 2026 (the “Expiration Time”). As of the Expiration Time, according to information provided by S&P Global Inc., the information and tabulation agent for the Consent Solicitation, the Issuer had received the requisite consents with respect to the Notes (the “Requisite Consents”) to effect the Proposed Amendments.

As previously announced, on October 23, 2026, Surgery Partners entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto, dated as of November 8, 2026, and as it may be further amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”) with Spyglass Topco, LLC (“Topco”), Spyglass Merger Subsidiary, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (“Merger Sub”), and, solely for the limited purposes set forth therein, Bon Secours Mercy Health, Inc. (“BSMH”). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into Surgery Partners, with Surgery Partners surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Topco (the “Merger”).

The Proposed Amendments will amend the Indenture to (i) provide that, concurrently with and following the consummation of the Merger in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date (as defined in the Merger Agreement), each of BSMH, HealthSpan Partners, a 501(c)(3) Ohio corporation affiliated with BSMH, and their respective affiliates, and certain groups of which any of them are members, will be “Permitted Holders” under the Indenture, in addition to the existing Permitted Holders, and (ii) add to, amend, supplement or change certain other defined terms in the Indenture related to the foregoing. Except for the Proposed Amendments, all existing terms of the Notes and the Indenture will remain unchanged, and the Proposed Amendments will not alter the Issuer’s obligation to pay the principal of or interest on the Notes or the stated interest rate or maturity date of the Notes.

The Issuer intends to execute a supplemental indenture to the Indenture setting forth the Proposed Amendments (the “Supplemental Indenture”) on or around November 24, 2026. The Supplemental Indenture will become effective upon its execution and delivery, but the Proposed Amendments will become operative only immediately prior to the consummation of the Merger, provided that the Consent Fee has been paid. Once operative, the Proposed Amendments will be binding on all Holders, including those that did not deliver consents. If the Consent Fee is paid but the Merger is not consummated on or prior to the date that is five business days after the End Date, the Proposed Amendments will not become operative, and Holders that received the Consent Fee will retain it.

Holders who validly delivered (and did not validly revoke) consents prior to the Expiration Time will receive a cash payment equal to $5.00 per $1,000 in principal amount of Notes for which such consents were delivered (the “Consent Fee”). The Issuer expects to pay the Consent Fee on November 24, 2026, whether or not the Merger is consummated.

Jefferies LLC acted as solicitation agent and S&P Global Inc. acted as information and tabulation agent in connection with the Consent Solicitation. Surgery Partners is a leading healthcare services company with a differentiated outpatient delivery model focused on providing high quality, cost effective solutions for surgical and related ancillary care in support of both patients and physicians. Sidus Space Expands Aerospace Customer Base with Argotec Order

Sidus extends nearly 15 years of aerospace manufacturing, proven on its own LizzieSat satellites in orbit, to a new international customer.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sidus Space, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIDU) ("Sidus" or the "Company"), a vertically integrated space and defense technology systems integrator, today announced it has secured a purchase order from new customer Argotec Group ("Argotec"), an international space company headquartered in Italy, with operations in Germany and the United States, including a technology hub in California and a second production facility in Melbourne, Florida. Under the purchase order, Sidus will manufacture cable assemblies supporting Argotec's HAWK satellite platform, with delivery expected in the first quarter of 2027.

Sidus designs, builds, and operates its own LizzieSat satellites, producing the cable harnesses, structures, and avionics that fly aboard them in its 35,000-square-foot facility in Cape Canaveral, Florida. That work is proven in orbit: LizzieSat-3 is currently hosting HEO USA's non-Earth imaging payload, which is actively capturing imagery. From the same facility, Sidus delivers end to end satellite infrastructure, mission-critical hardware, and technology integration including Fortis VPX – Maxima, an all-domain digital mission computing platform, all designed, built, tested, and operated in-house. Sidus has manufactured aerospace hardware for nearly 15 years and went public as a NASDAQ-listed company in 2021.

"We design and build the cable harnesses that fly on our own spacecraft, and that flight heritage is exactly what we now bring to other satellite manufacturers." said Carol Craig, Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Sidus Space. "Growing space companies need suppliers who have already solved these problems on their own spacecraft, and Argotec is the latest international company to put our experience to work, with U.S. operations just down the coast from our Cape Canaveral facility."

Argotec opened its first U.S. production facility, a Space Factory in Melbourne, Florida, near Kennedy Space Center, with an investment of more than $25 million, followed by the establishment of a technology hub in California dedicated to the development of telecommunications technologies. Both U.S. teams support government and commercial missions and will contribute to the continued growth of Argotec's presence in the United States. The company expects to triple the size of its U.S. teams over the next two years, expanding its capabilities and strengthening partnerships across the U.S. space ecosystem.

About Sidus Space  

Sidus Space®, Inc.  (NASDAQ: SIDU) is a vertically integrated space and defense technology company delivering satellite manufacturing and technology integration across all orbits, including LEO, GEO and lunar; all domain digital mission computing solutions; mission planning and management operations; AI enabling products and services; and space and defense hardware manufacturing. With its mission of Space Access Reimagined®, Sidus Space is committed to rapid innovation, adaptable solutions, and the optimization of space systems and data collection performance. With demonstrated space heritage, including designing, manufacturing and operating its own satellite and sensor system, LizzieSat®, Sidus Space serves government, defense, intelligence, and commercial customers around the globe. Strategically headquartered on Florida's Space Coast, Sidus Space operates a 35,000-square-foot space manufacturing, assembly, integration, and testing facility with direct access to nearby launch facilities. For more information, visit: sidusspace.com

About Argotec

Argotec is a space company with offices in Turin, Germany, and the United States. It specializes in manufacturing high-reliability small satellites and their subsystems for missions in low, medium, and geostationary Earth orbits, serving institutions, international agencies, government bodies, and civil protection authorities. In 2022, Argotec was the only company in the world to have two microsatellites operating in deep space as part of NASA's DART and Artemis I missions. Its current projects include HEO, the Earth observation constellation developed under Italy's IRIDE program; HENON, a mission to study solar storms and other space weather phenomena that can impact terrestrial and orbital critical infrastructure; and MiniCOR, a NASA program that will observe coronal mass ejections and the solar wind. Argotec also develops advanced dual-use technologies for inter-satellite cooperation, edge computing, and data intelligence, supporting security and monitoring programs across civil and defense applications. In 2024, Argotec inaugurated SpacePark, its highly automated production facility. In 2026, it opened its U.S. facility in Melbourne, Florida, and established a presence in California focused on telecommunications technologies. In October 2026, Argotec completed a €50 million capital increase through NUO Space S.p.A. The company is a leading player in the international New Space Economy and collaborates with partners worldwide.
